mechanism_narrative: The recent rise in WORKPLACES mobility will continue to feed discretionary stopovers and nearby shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks. The effect is strongest when WORKPLACES stays above its t-2w level for another week.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES does not remain elevated or RETAIL_REC does not average above the last 28 days over the next 28 days, this trend-signal hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT below a severe-decline regime indicates more mixed-purpose trips and more incidental shopping access, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks. If transit remains deeply suppressed, the retail effect will not materialize.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 2 percentage points week-on-week after being below -16%
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -16% or fails to improve week-on-week and RETAIL_REC still does not rise within two weeks, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve together, commuter flows generate the strongest uplift in retail visits through linked lunchtime and after-work purchases. The retail gain should appear over a four-week horizon and be weaker if only one of the two series improves.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not improve together, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent level crowds in everyday errand activity and spills over into adjacent retail-and-recreation visits. This should lift RETAIL_REC within one week, but only if grocery mobility remains strong.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above 25% for one full week
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM falls back below 25% and RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in PARKS mobility signals better outdoor conditions and higher general leisure participation, which should spill into retail and recreation visits over the next two to four weeks. The signal weakens if park mobility rebounds without a broader leisure rebound.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by 5 points from its latest weekly mean
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds by at least 5 points but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days, the seasonal spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, continued suppression of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES lowers city-center traffic and drags RETAIL_REC down within four weeks. The claim fails if mobility restrictions do not further depress both series.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below -10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES do not stay below -10% for two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior 28 days, the policy suppression hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES implies a split between staying home and commuting that compresses discretionary retail time. Under that pattern, RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next two weeks because trips become more utilitarian and less shopping-oriented.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES both increase week-on-week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES both rise but RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The recent improvement in RETAIL_REC should persist only if TRANSIT continues to recover from its depressed level; otherwise retail gains are temporary and will fade within four weeks. This is a persistence claim anchored on transport access rather than on one-off shopping demand.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves for at least two consecutive weeks from the current -14% level
failure_condition: If TRANSIT does not improve for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises sharply, or if RETAIL_REC falls despite continued transit recovery, the persistence mechanism fails.
